_why: BRIEF_GRAPH_2D5 §4, MEASURE 4 — the measure that decides. §4: 'Hand-read a sample of the extracted claims and report how many are real claims worth holding against how many are trivia, restatement, or the submission describing itself.' A large novelty count made of self-description is a WORSE outcome than top-down, not a better one.
_sample: 40 claims, every Nth by id from graph_claim_bottomup run bu1 — deterministic, so the same sample can be re-drawn and argued with. Reproduce: npx tsx position-graph/claims-bottomup.ts --handsample 40
_bar: REAL = a contestable assertion about the world, about cause, or about what should happen, that is worth holding in a queryable corpus. Not 'well written' — worth holding.
_reviewer: CC-Graph, 17 Aug 2026. ⚠ The same person who wrote the extraction prompt. An independent reader would be a better test and has not been run.

1.n: The hospice's position on assisted dying. ⚠ The model flagged it isAboutSelf; that flag is WRONG — an organisation stating its policy position is exactly what the corpus is for.

1297.n: 'Continuity is important, but more important for some patients than others' — this is the SCOPING that §2's second pass had to work to find on the same submission. Bottom-up caught it as a claim in its own right.

193.n: A strong empirical claim about what doctors think — the kind of thing the 83 propositions could never have asked for.

385.n: 'Swimming was the only sporting activity associated with a protective effect against falls' — specific, checkable, and on no proposition's list.

433.n: Thin — 'national leadership and funding are essential' — but contestable and policy-bearing. Counted real, marked weak.

961.n: 'Having in practice physio and pharmacist is great.' Barely a sentence, but an evaluative claim a reader could disagree with. Counted real, marked weak.

1057.n: Describes how this practice allocates patients. Not a claim about policy or the world.

673.n: ⚠ ARGUABLE. About the submitter's own 'Dance On' programme — but the second half ('underutilised due to fragmented commissioning and short-term funding') is a real policy claim. Scored strictly.

865.n: 'We intend to consult on this work in 2021.' Pure organisational housekeeping.

1825.n: ⚠ ARGUABLE. 'Funding for us to have an Ed Psych full time' is a genuine ask, but a single school's staffing is not a claim worth holding in a national corpus.

721.n: An example of good practice, offered as an example. Nothing contestable is asserted.

769.n: ⚠ THE ONE OUTRIGHT FAILURE. The quote is a bare bullet — 'Workforce development aligned to national standards.' — and the model supplied the verb ('is an enabler for system collaboration') that makes it read as a claim. The assertion is ours, not the submitter's. This is the bibliography failure of POSITION_SAMPLE.md Case 9 in a new costume: document structure invisible to the reader of a flat wall of text.
